significance: A Shiva temple at Thirukkuvalai in Nagapattinam district, about 15 km from Thiruvarur, revered in the 7th-century Tevaram hymns of Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar and counted among the Paadal Petra Sthalams. Its oldest masonry is 9th-century Chola work extended through the 16th century under the Thanjavur Nayaks; nineteen inscriptions record Chola, Pandya and Nayak endowments, and the temple is administered by the Dharmapuram Adheenam.
story: Legend holds that Brahma shaped the lingam here out of white sand, and that the nine planetary deities and Bhima came to the shrine to be absolved of their sins.
